item.title: Kepa Arrizabalaga admits Arsenal dressing room frustration after Borussia Dortmund Champions League draw despite stepping in for injured David Raya
item.description: Arsenal FC v Borussia Dortmund - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Kepa Arrizabalaga has opened up on the feeling of frustration inside the Arsenal dressing room following Tuesday's 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund. The Spanish goalkeeper was called into action at the Emirates Stadium after David Raya was sidelined with a shoulder problem. Stepping into the spotlight Arsenal maintained their unbeaten status in European competition this season, but the mood in North London was far from celebratory after a stalemate against the German giants . Kepa , who earned his first continental start of the campaign, found himself between the posts as Mikel Arteta’s side looked to solidify their position in the top eight of the league phase. The opportunity arose following a late injury blow to first-choice keeper David Raya , who sustained a shoulder issue during the weekend's Premier League clash with Newcastle United. The former Chelsea man performed well under pressure, but he admitted that the squad felt they had let two points slip away against the current Bundesliga leaders. Despite the quality of the opposition, the Gunners were the more dominant force for large periods of the contest. "We are a bit disappointed with the result," said Kepa on the club's official website . "I think it's a game that we should win, we created enough chances. I think we played very well against a very strong side. Sometimes football is like this, but if we keep playing like this, if we keep creating chances like this, I think we are in a good way." Dealing with late drama The atmosphere at the Emirates was electric as the home fans pushed for a decisive goal in the closing stages of the match. Arsenal threw everything forward in search of a winner, but the Dortmund defence held firm to secure a share of the spoils. For Kepa, the failure to find that late breakthrough was the primary source of the post-match disappointment within the camp. "We wanted the win, we were playing in front of our fans. Until the end, we pushed, the atmosphere was brilliant, I think we were very close. And when you don’t get that late goal, you are a bit frustrated, but I think we have to take the positives. I think we played very well, they are first in the Bundesliga. They are a really good team and I think we played them in a good way," the 32-year-old goalkeeper continued. Ready for the call Stepping in for Raya required a quick mental shift for Kepa, who has spent much of the season providing cover. However, the Spaniard insisted he was prepared for the challenge and was pleased to have the chance to contribute to the team’s European journey. He noted the difference between this start and other emergency appearances he has had to make in the past. "At least today I had a warm-up to go out!” he smiled when discussing the late change in the starting lineup. "But yeah, happy to be out there, happy to help the team. item.title: Wolves 3-0 Derby County - fans' verdicts
item.description: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Tuesday's Championship match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Derby County. Here are some of your comments: Wolves fans Alan: Our best team performance of the season. Yes, we still need to be more incisive with our finishing, but apart from a spirited opening 10 minutes by Derby we were never in trouble. Mane seems to have regained his confidence and for a small, young striker showed real strength in holding off a massive Derby defender to create the first goal. Armstrong was cool in taking his two goals and Tommy Doyle was superb in midfield. Andre, Krejci and Djiga were solid at the back and Trippier and Bueno were always dangerous on the wings. Fer Lopez is all energy despite having to cope with three of four defenders. Cesar's tactics are winning the fans over, what a change from the misery of last season. Peter: Despite the scoreline, poor finishing and decision-making in and around the box held Wolves back in a game they should have won 6-0. However, Cesar is forging a formidable team, arguably having at his disposal a squad with an outstanding depth of talented players who are technically the best in the Championship. Rob: Excellent all-round performance where the dominance translated into goals for once. The defensive midfield foundation of Andre and Doyle is a revelation and Mane had an excellent game. But we need to talk about Jordan James. He was instrumental in the last two goals by pulling the Derby midfield and defence all over the place. Our strongest team would include him starting somehow. Many have intimated Lopez is carrying an injury - if that is so, James could start in his stead whilst Peixoto works on a system that could include both of them as starters. Teams will then be pushed to keep both of them quiet and I believe there would be an even more sustainable uplift in performance. December's games will be a sterner test with better opposition but Wolves can be tougher and more ruthless on this evidence. [Cody Froggatt/Press Association] Derby fans Per: We are clearly not good enough for this league. Decent defending, but we kept losing the ball and hardly created any chances. We could have scored twice (Morris and Fuseini) in the opening minutes, but we didn't take our chances and in the end we were outplayed. Philip: Absolutely awful. Route one or misplaced passes trying to play out from the back. Completely lacking in confidence. I really am not sure if Eustace can dig us out of this rut. I'd like to hope he can but I'm really not sure. Dave: Heart and fight is missing in this team. Understand the issues the proposed takeover has caused and the injuries, but our goalkeeper, who's been injured himself, is our top player too often. Need to get stuck in and get their hands dirty.

item.title: Fairfield Union’s Andy Clark is the 2025 Eagle-Gazette Coach of the Year
item.description: LANCASTER — When this year’s group of Fairfield Union football seniors were in the seventh grade, they won one game, going 1-7. Fairfield Union coach Andy Clark refused to give up on them. He believed in them and raised their standard and refused to let them fall below it. The group steadily improved and they started winning, but this season was special. The Falcons showed a lot of perseverance, stuck together when things looked bleak, and came out on the side as champions. Clark helped lead Fairfield Union to its first Mid-State League-Buckeye Division championship in 20 years. Playing Hamilton Township in a must-win situation in Week 10 to gain a share of the league title, the Falcons were able to hold on for a 14-6 victory. Fairfield Union picked up its first-ever playoff win in 2025, qualified for the playoffs again this season and hosted a first-round game. The Falcons finished with a 6-1 league mark and went 8-3 overall. Because of his leadership, Clark is the 2026 Eagle-Gazette Football Coach of the Year. More: Fairfield Union clinches a share of the Mid-State League-Buckeye title He was thankful for the recognition but wanted to talk more about what the team accomplished and how their hard work enabled them to achieve what they did. “Football is the most team-oriented sport on planet Earth, so anytime individual awards are given out, it’s clearly a group effort,” Clark said. “You have to have players that have bought in. They set goals, and they worked to achieve those. For that to happen, a lot of good things had to be in place, and that’s what makes it the most rewarding.” What made it even more special for Clark was how far the team had come, especially the seniors. “It was a group that could have given up on themselves and each other, but they stuck together,” Clark said. “They continued to work hard, they pushed each other, and they have a tight bond. They shared in all that pain and disappointment when they were younger, and even early in their high school careers. They really worked their tails off and made improvements each year, and it led to this year. They were playing big games at the end of the season, and I don’t know without that tough beginning they would be where they are now. They dealt with a lot of adversity in their careers. It’s just a testament to them sticking together.” The fact that the Falcons were able to hang on and pull out such a huge victory over the Rangers in the last game of the regular season, with so much on the line, it all went back to Clark holding his team to a higher standard and the belief they could win big games. “They were so prepared for that game, and they were locked in,” Clark said. “It was just neat to see it all come together. I was happy for them to see how far they had come to get to that moment with so much on the line. It was so gratifying to see them celebrate after that game. It all went back to holding them to the standard that it takes to achieve the goals they wanted to achieve.

When he steps between the lines, he becomes a wrecking machine, making tackles from sideline to sideline and punishing running backs and quarterbacks. At 6-foot-3, 210 pounds, Reynolds trained hard to get his body in the best shape it could be, and it paid off. He had a tremendous season and made his presence felt immediately by averaging double-digit tackles for the Golden Gales. Reynolds finished with a team-leading 113 total tackles, including 60 solos, 12 tackles for loss, a forced fumble, five pass breakups and a blocked kick. Thanks to his tremendous season, Reynolds was an obvious choice to be selected as the 2026 Eagle-Gazette Defensive Player of the Year. item.description: LANCASTER — Fairfield Union quarterback Dean Clark has that it factor. He is the type of player coaches love to coach. His teammates gravitate toward him and follow his lead. Clark was the clear-cut leader of the Falcons, and while he hasn’t always been the most vocal, he knew he had to be that guy to speak up and be that one player that each member of the team looked to, especially when things weren't going well. As it turned out, Clark is a natural leader and his confidence and belief fed into the whole team. A year after qualifying and winning their first-ever playoff game in school history, Clark and the Falcons had loftier goals this season. He helped lead Fairfield Union to a share of the Mid-State League-Buckeye Division championship, the school’s first league title in 20 years. Clark had an outstanding season as he led the Falcons to an 8-3 overall record. He accounted for 1,888 total yards and 21 touchdowns. He completed 79-of-128 passes for 1,337 yards and 15 touchdowns and rushed 114 times for 551 yards and six touchdowns. For his efforts, Clark was chosen as the 2026 Eagle-Gazette Offensive Player of the Year. More: Fairfield Union clinches a share of the Mid-State League-Buckeye title “It is a gratifying feeling,” Clark said of winning the player of the year award. “There are a lot of great players in the area, so receiving this recognition is special. item.title: Alabama’s Nate Oats stays silent on LSU-SEC standoff, but rips ‘hypocritical’ coaches
item.description: David Leong-Imagn Images Alabama’s Nate Oats stays silent on LSU-SEC standoff, but rips ‘hypocritical’ coaches appeared first on ClutchPoints . People seldom feel sorry for Alabama, or any SEC school for that matter, but Crimson Tide basketball head coach Nate Oats is more convinced than ever that his program was wrongfully criticized for putting former G League player Charles Bediako on the roster last season. He takes serious issue with the villain narrative that swirled around Tuscaloosa, especially since eligibility controversy is quite commonplace now. Oats was already not in a great mood following his team’s 68-63 Players Era 16 loss versus Baylor, so what better way to blow off steam than by dwelling on the past and taking shots at his contemporaries . “A lot of those coaches wanted to speak on the Bediako thing, well, they’re doing the exact thing this year,” the two-time SEC champion said from Las Vegas, Nevada’s T-Mobile Arena, per BamaCentral’s Theodore Fernandez. “Yeah, it does bother me. They’re kind of hypocritical, to be honest with you.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Oats refrained from commenting on LSU, as the university faces possible expulsion from the SEC amid the league’s ongoing dispute with RJ Luis Jr. He had no problem snapping back against all the anti-Alabama rhetoric, however. The former SEC Coach of the Year believes he was unfairly condemned for taking advantage of the system, particularly because others are now following his lead. That being said, he may be forgetting just how unusual the Bediako situation was. The Canadian big man returned to Alabama last season after being out of college for almost three years. He played in the G League and therefore brought with him a competitive edge. Surprisingly, Charles Bediako did not make a huge impact in his second stint with the Tide. He averaged only 10.0 points and 4.6 rebounds across five games before being denied eligibility. It was hard to believe he made it that far. Despite a fairly blatant circumvention of collegiate athletic ethics, Alabama was not in danger of being ousted from the conference. LSU is not a victim, either, to be clear, but this notion that the Crimson Tide were mercilessly ripped apart ignores certain context. While Alabama basketball received significant backlash, it did not face severe consequences. Nate Oats is nevertheless annoyed and is taking the opportunity to speak his mind. Perhaps the Tide can unleash that frustration on the court, as they try to bounce back against Kansas State on Thanksgiving. item.title: Opel and Citroen exit is not a betrayal of Formula E, but a major blow at the worst possible time
item.description: Motorsport photo What many had feared has unfortunately come to pass. In light of the substantial financial hole that emerged at the end of 2025 and the losses recorded in the third quarter of this year, Stellantis has decided to close almost all of its programmes, including those in Formula E, which at the end of 2027 will lose Citroen and Opel. However, it is important to understand that this decision goes beyond a single category and is not a barometer of the championship's health. This is not a betrayal of Formula E, of what it represents or its value, as the simultaneous departure from the WEC with Peugeot shows. Rather, it is a reflection of the very complex moment the entire European automotive sector is going through. Read Also: Peugeot quits WEC, Citroen and Opel to wind down Formula E programmes Stellantis has not yet reported its full financial results for 2026, with the latest statement currently stopping at the third-quarter losses, but the company's senior management has repeatedly said that in 2027 the rising price of raw materials could cost not millions, but billions. The exit from racing programmes starts here: the problem is not motorsport, but what lies upstream. On the contrary, Formula E was conceived as a financially sustainable category, precisely to attract the major manufacturers. It is a model that worked for years, to the point that today there is no shortage of leading brands. However, for a series whose main strength is in manufacturers' commitment, losing two brands in one go is the equivalent of a well-placed right hook. It is easy to understand why sporting projects are the first to be cut in difficult times, but both Opel and Citroen have already invested a significant part of the budget allocated to the 2027 season, so much so that they will contest the season. The economic effects of this decision, therefore, will not be immediate, not to mention the penalties that will have to be paid to Formula E linked to the early exit from the championship. “Formula E will work closely with Stellantis to manage an orderly transition, also addressing the contractual obligations and financial aspects linked to the early exit, while it will continue to assess the strong interest shown by new manufacturers and teams intending to join the grid in the coming seasons,” read a statement released by the electric series. item.title: Como join the Serie A sides eyeing January move for Joshua Zirkzee
item.description: Como join the Serie A sides eyeing January move for Joshua Zirkzee Como have joined the growing list of Serie A sides interested in signing Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee during the January transfer window. Zirkzee is a transfer target for a number of Italian clubs after struggling for favour at Old Trafford. The Dutchman has not started a Premier League game this season and has failed to earn a regular role under multiple managers, with Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick all unconvinced. He has continued to be overlooked this season, despite Benjamin Sesko’s absence through injury. The Slovenian striker has been ruled out until January, but that has not aided Zirkzee’s quest for minutes. Zirkzee is expected to hold talks with Mauricio Pochettino about his status in the new manager’s plans, though there’s an expectation that he will be allowed to leave. According to Sky Sports , Como have joined Napoli in leading the chase for the 25-year-old. Zirkzee had an impressive Serie A spell prior to moving to the Premier League and was named the division’s Young Player of the Season after scoring 11 league goals for Bologna in 2023/24. Roma and Juventus have also tracked Zirkzee, who was a target for Everton on summer Deadline Day, but United rejected the loan offer late in the window. item.title: Taylor Lewan thinks Caleb Williams could do what no NFL player has ever done before
item.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images Caleb Williams is only in the midst of his third season in the NFL but he is already being touted to achieve big things. The young quarterback suffered a hamstring strain back in September but has since shone upon his return to help the Chicago Bears go 8-2. Amid his impressive form, Taylor Lewan has now floated the idea that Williams could be named the NFL MVP and win the Comeback Player of the Year award in 2026. Speaking via a podcast this week, he said: “Caleb Williams, though. Tell you what, stud. MVP-calibre guy. Comeback Player of the Year in the same year.” One of his fellow hosts then pointed out: “Yep. That would be the first time ever,” to which Lewan responded: “That would be unbelievable. He’s a phenomenal quarterback and talent.” How Caleb Williams compares to other MVP candidates Because of his injury, Williams has only played seven games so far this season. So, it is hard to judge him on overall stats like passing yards, which he ranks 25th in the league for with 1,727, and passing touchdowns, which he ranks 19th for (10) When it comes to per game stats, the Bears ace has a 68.3% completion rate, which is the eighth-highest in the NFL and below several MVP candidates like Joe Burrow (74.2%) and Brock Purdy (71.0%). Elsewhere, he is throwing for 246.7 yards per game. That is the 11th-highest total in the league but again, still off the pace of big names like Purdy (262.4), Burrow (309.5), Patrick Mahomes (270.9) and Jordan Love (283.8). Williams’ average yards per pass attempt isn’t that amazing either. His 7.9 average (10th overall) puts him below Lamar Jackson (10.0), Purdy (9.0), Trevor Lawrence (8.4), Josh Allen (8.4), Burrow (8.1) and more. So, while he is having a good season and should have plenty of years ahead of him in the NFL to keep getting better, he doesn’t really look to be on the same level as other top quarterbacks just yet. item.description: Arsenal told to pay £100m to sign rival’s attacker Bournemouth Stand Firm on Eli Junior Kroupi as Manchester United Weigh Nathan Collins Move Manchester United’s search for experience and leadership in defence is gathering pace ahead of January, with TALKSPORT reporting that Brentford captain Nathan Collins is prominent on the club’s shortlist. The 25-year-old has emerged as a leading domestic option as Mauricio Pochettino looks to address a damaging start to the season and a back line that has become a major concern inside Old Trafford. United’s recruitment team are understood to be exploring the home market for players who can arrive with minimal adaptation time. Collins appeals on that front, both for his Premier League experience and his standing at Brentford. Fulham’s Calvin Bassey has also been considered, although expectations are that he will commit to a new contract, while Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite remains admired but is viewed as a difficult deal to execute in the middle of the campaign, largely because of cost. Photo IMAGO Manchester United Defensive Overhaul Moves Forward The urgency around United’s plans appears to have accelerated. What had been shaping up as a summer rebuild in defence now looks increasingly likely to be brought forward. With Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martinez all due to be out of contract next summer, there had already been a strategic review of the department. However, the scale of the team’s defensive issues has forced a rethink. Conceding 34 goals already, a total described as the worst across Europe’s top five leagues, has sharpened minds at board level. That context explains why Collins is being discussed so seriously, even if Brentford are highly likely to insist on a substantial fee. item.title: Marshall Faulk shared his Parkinson's diagnosis for one selfless reason | Opinion
item.description: BATON ROUGE, La. – Eric Dickerson warned him. After Marshall Faulk hung up his spikes following an amazing 12-year career as one of the greatest running backs in NFL history, Dickerson told him what to expect as a former football player in retirement. Those old football injuries, Dickerson cautioned, never really go away. “Eric warned me,” Faulk, 53, told USA TODAY Sports during a wide-ranging interview in his office at Southern University , where he is winding down his first season as a rookie head coach. "Like when I retired, I think I was 33, he said, 'When you get to be 43 or 48, check back with me then.'" It brought back the memory of a conversation I had a few years ago with Dickerson, himself one of the greatest running backs ever, when he mentioned how difficult it was for him to get a good night’s sleep. He told me about nagging aches from various injuries – including from a shot he took in the chest from a late hit after scoring a touchdown decades ago – that sometimes popped up from nowhere. When I told Faulk about my chat with his fellow Hall of Famer, he grinned and nodded. “That is so true,” Faulk said. “I think at 48, I tore my Achilles. I was like, ‘Damn!’ ” What were you doing? “Nothing, man, nothing. Seriously.” You weren’t on the golf course? “Nothing. Literally, I took a step down. Pop. Nothing,” Faulk described. MORE JARRETT BELL: Forget Parkinson's. Marshall Faulk is building a football power at Southern | Exclusive Why Marshall Faulk revealed Parkinson's diagnosis The foot has long been fully healed, yet Faulk has gone public with his current health challenge. He recently revealed that he was diagnosed about a year-and-half ago with the early stages of Parkinson’s disease. He’s so upbeat about his prospects for managing this – which includes medication – and that he has had no progressive symptoms. According to experts, Parkinson’s is considered a risk factor, but not a direct cause, for neurological decline. Still, it may be natural to wonder – on the heels of former All-Pro running back Chris Johnson’s disclosure in July that he is battling ALS , which has robbed him of his ability to speak and left him bound to a wheelchair; and with former running back Roger Craig using his Hall of Fame induction speech in August to announce that he has been dealing with vascular dementia – whether Faulk’s Parkinson’s diagnosis is linked to football. The same shocks to the body absorbed in football that can blow out knees and dislocate ankles, for example, can also rattle brains. Faulk’s discovery began on the golf course, when stiffness in joints prompted him to seek evaluation. “You know, I have some stiffness in my wrist, my hand, my elbow,” he said. “At times, it would just freeze up. I thought, ‘Hey, that’s par for the course. I played professional football.’ And then to find out it’s something else, it’s like, ‘OK, yeah.’ ” Marshall Faulk NFL career stats Faulk was 33 when he played his final season with the St. Louis Rams in 2005

item.title: ‘Let them learn’ – Why Peyton Manning is desperate for young QBs to break his rookie record
item.description: Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images Peyton Manning had a historic rookie year filled with record-setting numbers, but the Broncos and Colts legend is ready to pass the mantle on to a new young quarterback. Manning’s 1998 rookie season was phenomenal, as he set five new records as a rookie quarterback in what many consider the most dominant debut season in NFL history. However, of those five records, only one stands to this day, and Manning is just waiting for the day a young quarterback snatches that record from him. Peyton Manning once revealed the real reason he wants his NFL rookie record broken During an appearance on the Kittle Things podcast a few months ago, Peyton Manning jokingly explained to George Kittle why he is ready for his last remaining record from his rookie year – the record for most interceptions thrown by a rookie – to be broken. He noted that coaches don’t allow their rookie quarterbacks to make mistakes and stay in the game, and that is standing in the way of his record possibly being broken. “Am I proud to hold the NFL interception rookie record? No,” Manning said on Kittle’s podcast earlier this year. “Would I like to get it broken? Yes. Do I think it should be with 17 games now? Yes. Do the coaches take the rookies that are struggling out too early? 100%. “Leave them in there. Let them learn. I’m over it, as you can tell. But that would be my rookie mistake. Respect it, but don’t over-respect it where you kind of get yourself out of whack.” For those unaware, Manning currently holds the record for the most interceptions thrown by a rookie quarterback in a single season with 28. In fact, Manning set five records in his rookie year – most interceptions thrown, most attempts, most completed passes, most passing yards, and most passing touchdowns. Out of these records, all except his interceptions record have been broken, with his completed passes and passing touchdowns thrown records being the last to stand till Justin Herbert broke both of them in the 2020 season. item.title: Michael Redd gives ‘monster’ Karl-Anthony Towns his flowers for powerful start
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images The New York Knicks haven’t had the perfect start to the 2026-27 NBA season, but one ex-NBA All-Star has highlighted how good Karl-Anthony Towns has been. The New York Knicks had a bit of championship hangover to start the 2026-27 NBA season. The reigning champs won six and lost six of their first 12 games, but have since won five straight. While stars on the team like Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby have struggled, one player is on fire. Karl-Anthony Towns was instrumental in helping the Knicks win it all last season. And despite the struggles of his teammates, he is performing at an elite level. Towns is leading the entire league in rebounding, and has notched double-doubles in every single one of the 16 games he has played. And finally, someone is ready to show him some love. Michael Redd says Karl-Anthony Towns should be praised for the ‘player he is’ after excellent start Towns is averaging 21.8 points, 13.9 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 16 appearances for the Knicks, shooting 54.3 percent from the field and 41.5 percent from three-point range. He has been effective on both ends of the floor, and has been performing consistently well. Former Milwaukee Bucks star Michael Redd has now highlighted KAT’s start to the season, showering him with some well-deserved praise. “Easy to call KAT’s season a championship high,” Redd wrote in an X post. “We’ve seen that movie before. A guy has a monster June, gets marketed all summer, then the season tips and he crashes right back to earth. Happens every year. Look around his own locker room, a couple faces of that title run came out ice cold, one even got benched. “Not KAT. Dude never dipped. Leading the whole NBA in rebounds, career-long double-double streak, scoring as efficient as he’s ever been. Are we actually watching his (really high) ceiling right now? Because if this is it, wow. The man has gotten so, so good. “We spend so much time talking about what he isn’t that we forget to give him flowers for the incredible player and man that he is. KAT’s having a monster year, in the middle of a heck of a career, and we get to watch it happen. Appreciate it while it’s here. Because it’s powerful!” This is a fantastic sentiment from Redd, and one that is sure to resonate with Knicks fans. Towns is also performing in a way that will make it difficult for New York to not pay him soon. He could be a free agent at the end of this season, and his greatness to start the year might just see him get paid. item.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images San Antonio Spurs legend Sean Elliott has dismissed the Los Angeles Lakers’ championship chances, insisting Luka Doncic and his teammates are not good enough to win the NBA title. Elliott, a 1999 NBA champion, questioned whether a team can build a championship-winning side around a player who dominates possession as much as Doncic. The comments come ahead of a major NBA Cup meeting between the Lakers and Spurs, who currently share identical records at the top of the Western Conference. Sean Elliott questions Los Angeles Lakers’ championship credentials ahead of San Antonio Spurs clash Speaking after San Antonio’s game against the Utah Jazz, Elliott made his feelings about the Lakers’ title chances clear. “Well, the Lakers aren’t gonna win the NBA championship. They’re not,” the Spurs colour commentator said. I like [Sandro Mamukelashvili] in a Laker uniform.” Elliott also highlighted Doncic’s defensive contributions as a concern, arguing that a team’s best player must be effective at both ends of the court. “Plus, your best player always, he’s gotta be a stalwart on the defensive end of the floor,” he said. “I firmly believe that.” His criticism also focused on Doncic’s usage rate, which currently stands at a league-leading 39 per cent. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
